subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A short story is a work of fiction that is typically under 10,000 words.
• A novella is a work of fiction that is longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.
• "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" is a 25,000-word novella by Robert Louis Stevenson.
• "A Christmas Carol" is a 28,000-word novella by Charles Dickens.
prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about novellas. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Examples of novellas include "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" by Robert Louis Stevenson and "A Christmas Carol" by Charles Dickens.
choices.B: A short story is typically under 10,000 words, but "A Christmas Carol," at 28,000 words, is much longer.
choices.C: Novellas are works of fiction that are longer than short stories but shorter than novels.
choices.D: While "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" is 25,000 words, "A Christmas Carol" is 28,000 words.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. This choice makes a supported generalization about novellas based on the note that a novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. This choice compares short stories in general to one specific novella but doesn't say anything about novellas as a category.
